summary.tldr: Bill C-22 updates rules for police and CSIS to get data and information during investigations, creates a provider framework, and sets a parliamentary review.
what_it_does: Amends the Criminal Code to make it easier to get basic information, subscriber information, tracking data, transmission data and computer data during investigations.
Clarifies when peace officers and public officers can use information that is voluntarily provided, publicly available, or obtained in exigent circumstances.
Allows judges and justices to authorize requests to foreign telecom providers for transmission data or subscriber information they hold.
Amends the Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters Act so the Minister of Justice can authorize enforcement of certain foreign production decisions in Canada.
Amends the Canadian Security Intelligence Service Act to help CSIS get basic information and to clarify response times for production orders.

Enacts the Supporting Authorized Access to Information Act, which sets a framework for electronic service providers to help authorized persons exercise access powers under the Criminal Code and the CSIS Act.
who_it_affects: People whose data may be requested
summary.background: Bill C-22 was introduced in the House of Commons on 12 March 2026 and received first reading. Part 3 provides for parliamentary review of Parts 1 and 2.
